results.evidence: The contradiction is real: the permit field names a Wild Sky Wilderness self-issue permit while access.permit says no permit. Wild Sky Wilderness lies north of Index and Skykomish with the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness adjoining it to the east, so Spinnaker (on the crest just north of Stevens Pass) is not in Wild Sky. Whether the summit lies inside the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness could not be settled: the Forest Service PCT page says the trail enters that wilderness about three miles north of Stevens Pass, while other sources put the boundary near Lake Valhalla (~5 mi). The summit is in King County (west side, Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF) while the Yodelin approach is in Chelan County (Okanogan-Wenatchee NF), so access.landManager is right for the trailhead and not for the summit. Needs a boundary-map check before any patch.

results.fact: Best season for climbing Spinnaker Peak
results.correct_value: A winter/spring snow climb, roughly Dec-Apr; summer is a brush bushwhack
results.evidence: The peak's own route page describes Spinnaker as a winter off-trail objective and says it is not a good summer destination because the vegetation makes the off-trail bushwhack intense. An independent trip write-up describes a snowshoe ascent via Yodelin and the ridge past Point 5261 in winter/early-spring conditions. seasonal_guidance, the seasonal_hazards weather/avalanche months and the crowds text had been copied from a summer scramble and are rewritten to the snow season; the season chip is trimmed to its window.

results.evidence: gain_ft 2045 is simply the net difference between the 3,600 ft trailhead and the ~5,645 ft summit (the range one trip write-up quotes); the route drops to Nason Creek and adds the Martin Peak side trip, so cumulative gain is higher. The companion Martin Peak page gives about 2,500 ft of gain for the double-summit outing, matching loss_ft, both itinerary gainFt/lossFt and totalNote on the row.

dist_km 12.5 km equals 7.8 mi, the round-trip figure (also the itinerary's miles), but the field renders as the one-way approach. Trip write-ups give 7.8 mi round trip and 7.3 mi round trip for Spinnaker with Martin, so one way is about 3.7-3.9 mi; the summit waypoint sits at 3.6 mi.

high_point_ft says 5,645 ft while the summit waypoint, itinerary schedule and objective say 5,654 ft. One trip write-up gives an elevation range topping out at 5,645 ft; no second topo-derived source could be fetched (the peak databases returned 403), so the 9 ft split is left open.

Real: best_season and seasonal_guidance run to October, past the season chip's Sep. Ascents/attempts found are in June (2001, 2005, 2013) and September (2015), supporting Jun-Sep, but no source was found that confirms or rules out October as part of the climbing season, so neither side is changed.

Sources genuinely split. The Mountaineers route description gives the bolt-protected friction face as 5.6 moves, and a 2015 trip report calls it 'a couple 5.6 moves'. Wikipedia gives the easiest route as 5.3, and a 2001 attempt report says the blank face is 'reported to be 5.3' (both likely from the older guidebook grade). No source supports the 5.4 in climbing_route. The grade column ('Grade II, Class 3 to 4') also disagrees with the 5.6 rock_grade; whichever grade is adopted, grade, rock_grade, pitch_detail[0], climbing_route[2], hazards[1], overview, beta, descent_text, pro_tips[3], approach_variants hazards and the itinerary day-2 text must be aligned together.

Real: rappels implies one rap on a single 60 m rope, descent_text two (maybe three) and climbing_route three. A Mountaineers trip report describes one double-rope rappel over an overhang; another describes rappelling the slab using trees; the Mountaineers route page says only 'rappel and downclimb'. That supports one rap with two ropes, but nothing settles the single-60 m count.

Round trips found: about 17 mi / 7,300 ft via Snow Lakes trail (trip report summary) and about 18 mi / 7,400 ft with a Temple Canyon camp (2001 report). The row's 16-16.5 mi (approach, turnaround, hazards, itinerary.cal, totalNote car-to-car) and 19-20 mi (3-day totalNote) bracket these; the waypoints' Prusik Pass at 9.5 mi appear to describe a different approach (via the Core) than Temple Canyon. No single figure is confirmed by two sources, so nothing is changed.

gain_ft 8,000 and loss_ft 6,995 (the net trailhead-to-summit difference) disagree with each other and with the itinerary's 7,200 ft total gain/loss. Reports give about 7,300 ft and about 7,400 ft; close but not one agreed value, so left for a decision.
